subject: String names with spaces in plyr

messages.author: 9c9b5f9c6aaa025d
messages.subject: String names with spaces in plyr
parts:
Hello,
I am wondering if it is possible to use plyr with string names with spaces, or I should say, wondering if there is a reason you cannot. For example,

> library(plyr)
> df <- data.frame(x=c(1,2,2), "y z" = c(6,6,9), check.names = FALSE)
> ddply(df, .(`y z`), sum)
  y z V1
1   6 15
2   9 11
> ddply(df, "y z", sum)  
Error in parse(text = x) : <text>:1:3: unexpected symbol
1: y z
     ^

The reason this comes up for me is that I have a bunch of data that I would prefer to deal with in spaces. I would like to be able to store the column name in a variable and reference it in both plyr and general references, e.g., 
> my_col <- "y z"
> df[[my_col]]
> ddply(df, my_col, sum)

Thanks!
Doug

messages.subject: Re: String names with spaces in plyr
parts:
On Aug 9, 2012, at 6:29 PM, Brandon Hurr wrote:

can you paste() "`a b`"?

Certainly easy enough to test:
> paste('`a b`')
[1] "`a b`"
I think the issue is that he might not know what his variable names are and he wants to SAC with plyr, but can't with a col.name that contains a space.

"SAC"? Save A Cayestroke?

The names do get coerced to character values:

> a <- data.frame(`b a`=1, check.names=F)
> names(a) == "`b a`"
[1] FALSE

Usually I get around this by allowing check.names=T and using sub() to swap "." for " " when I later create a plot from the data.

messages.subject: Re: String names with spaces in plyr
parts: What's wrong with "`a b`" ?

The reason this does not work for me is because I can't use that in a general reference to a data.frame (though it does work in plyr):
> my_col="`y z`"

> ddply(df, my_col, sum)
  y z V1
1   6 15
2   9 11

> df[[my_col]]
NULL
Usually I get around this by allowing check.names=T and using sub() to swap "." for " " when I later create a plot from the data.

Yes, good suggestion, though not ideal. One of the nuances for me that I will also deal with here is that my column names are not always just spaces but can also have parens that are converted to dots by check.names = TRUE, so a simple sub does not work. I need to carry around the original names() and do something like names(df) <- original_names before creating anything external.

From Hadley's earlier response, it does not look like plyr will be able to accept strings with spaces. So, it seems like I should store the original  (check.names = FALSE) names in a vector, convert the names using check.names = TRUE so I can use everything in a string in both calls to plyr and the data.frame, and then rename the columns before doing anything external, like writing results to csv or plots. 

Thanks for everyone's help, and please let me know if you see any alternatives.

Best wishes,
Doug

messages.subject: Re: String names with spaces in plyr
parts:
> From Hadley's earlier response, it does not look like plyr will be able to
> accept strings with spaces. So, it seems like I should store the original
> (check.names = FALSE) names in a vector, convert the names using check.names
> = TRUE so I can use everything in a string in both calls to plyr and the
> data.frame, and then rename the columns before doing anything external, like
> writing results to csv or plots.

The problem is not that plyr doesn't accept strings with spaces (which
it does), it's that it uses a different way of doing it to base R.
It's hard to know why that's a problem without understanding the rest
of your workflow.

messages.author: 9c9b5f9c6aaa025d
messages.subject: Re: String names with spaces in plyr
parts:
> The problem is not that plyr doesn't accept strings with spaces (which
> it does), it's that it uses a different way of doing it to base R.
> It's hard to know why that's a problem without understanding the rest
> of your workflow.

Sure, here is my workflow:
1) I get a csv in from an external data source. Most of the columns
have spaces in them, or even parentheses (note, I have no control what-
so-ever on variable naming from the raw data source).
2) I read the file into R using read.csv. (I have been using
check.names = TRUE so far but that is what I am trying to get around
here and start using check.names = FALSE)
3) I manipulate the data in some way, e.g., adding two columns of the
data.frame together to create a new column of data in the same
data.frame
4) I plyr the data to do something interesting
5) I write the data.frame to file or graphic

The important part to me is that my external data sources sends me
multiple separate csv files, most of which have the same column name
in them. For example, I get up to 20 reports that have something like
"Sale quantity" in them - all representing the same concept but
conjoined with different variables. Unfortunately, my external data
source has a propensity to change the column names on me unexpectedly,
e.g. changing to "Sales quantity". What I would like to do is create a
master variable that is something like:
> QUANTITY <- "Sale quantity"
that could then be used in my code as I have described before, e.g.:
df$quantity_per_person <- df[[QUANTITY]] / df[[NUMBER_OF_PEOPLE]]
ddply(df, QUANTITY, sum) # obviously not this, but something like it

Then, when my client changes the variable name on me, I just change:
> QUANTITY <- "Sales quantity"
and I am done. I am not going through multiple files and lines of code
doing a find and replace on df$Sale.quantity into df$Sales.quantity,
or alternatively changing the plyr calls in a similar fashion.

Make sense? Thanks again for everyone's help!

messages.author: 9c9b5f9c6aaa025d
messages.subject: Re: String names with spaces in plyr
parts:
Hey everyone,
After mulling this over a bit more and a very helpful suggestions from
Winston Chang, here is my current thinking on this: I define my own
function that is similar to . that will convert strings to back-quoted
strings. I like this solution best because I don't have to carry
around "R names" and "pretty names."

Using my example from before, here is what my code will now look like:
> df <- data.frame(x=c(1,2,2), "y z" = c(6,6,9), check.names = FALSE)

> s <- "y z"
> `..` <- function(x){return(paste0("`", x, "`"))}
> df[[s]]
[1] 6 6 9
> ddply(df, ..(s), sum)

Does anyone see any major issues with this approach? For now I will
just define .. in my personal utils package. Perhaps, Hadley, this
could be added to the plyr package?

Thanks again everyone!
Doug

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: String names with spaces in plyr
parts:
> Hadley, plyr doesn't accept spaces the same way that base R does -- is
> this a bug or a feature? That is, is there any reason to not make plyr
> behave the same way?

Currently you can do:

.(x = min(x))

and exactly equivalent

c(x = "min(x)")

I don't know if this is a feature that anyone uses, but it's there. It
would be trivial to change it so that c(x = "min(x)") is equivalent to
c(x = `min(x)`)

Hadley
